goals: Quantify spatial variability of recharge across elevation and soil gradients
Validate simulated water table depth against USGS wells and Fan 2013 prior
Test the published claim of uniform 500 mm/yr recharge
key_processes: Water balance partitioning (P - ET - runoff = recharge)
Elevation control on precipitation and snow accumulation/melt
Soil control on infiltration and subsurface drainage
Water table dynamics and aquifer storage

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM can simulate the water balance and subsurface drainage (QDRAI = recharge proxy) at stratified locations across the heterogeneous domain. Spatial sampling across elevation and soil gradients tests whether recharge is uniform or varies systematically.

answerable: Soil texture control on infiltration and recharge via SSURGO-derived hydraulic properties
Water table depth validation against USGS wells and Fan 2013 prior (co-located comparison)
Forcing period effects on recharge (interannual variability 1980-2018)
Snow accumulation and melt processes (H2OSNO, QSNOMELT in default output)

not_answerable.aspect: Fine-scale (<12 km) elevation control on precipitation and recharge
not_answerable.why: NLDAS forcing is 0.125° (~12 km) resolution with no within-cell elevation lapse rate. Sub-12 km terrain (e.g. ridgetop vs valley) is unresolved. NLDAS does provide orographic variation across the 1625 m basin relief (verified ~15 distinct precip values), but local gradients are smoothed.
not_answerable.needs: Sub-12 km elevation-downscaled forcing (e.g. 1-4 km WRF or statistical downscaling with lapse rates)

not_answerable.why: No recharge measurements are available in-domain (observations_missing lists recharge). Recharge is inferred from model output (QDRAI) but cannot be validated against observations.
not_answerable.needs: In-situ recharge measurements (lysimeters, tracer studies, or water balance closure at gaged sub-basins)

not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral transport or routing. Cannot aggregate recharge to basin total or compare to streamflow-derived recharge estimates.
not_answerable.needs: Runoff routing and aggregation tool, or streamflow gage data with baseflow separation

bands: high: 1400-1977 m (snow-dominated, shorter growing season, higher P)

classes: coarse-textured / well-drained (high infiltration, low storage, higher recharge potential)
fine-textured / poorly-drained (low infiltration, high storage, lower recharge potential)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands × 2 soil classes = 6 strata. Sample 2 columns per stratum to resolve the factorial design and provide light replication. Total 12 exploratory columns spans the driver space without oversampling.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Distribute columns across the elevation-soil strata to avoid spatial clustering. Within each stratum, select locations representative of the dominant land cover (likely forest). Avoid urban areas, water bodies, and steep slopes where 1-D assumptions break down. Validation columns are pinned to USGS well locations (not chosen by stratification).
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 columns per stratum provides minimal replication to assess within-stratum variability and guard against single-point anomalies (e.g. local soil mapping errors).

sampling_plan.reason: Rain-dominated, high infiltration: tests baseline recharge in warm, well-drained lowlands
Rain-dominated, low infiltration: tests runoff vs recharge partitioning in poorly-drained lowlands
Rain-snow transition, high infiltration: tests snowmelt recharge pulse in well-drained mid-slopes
Rain-snow transition, low infiltration: tests soil limitation on snowmelt infiltration
Snow-dominated, high infiltration: tests maximum recharge potential from deep snowpack melt
Snow-dominated, low infiltration: tests soil constraint on high-elevation recharge despite high P
Co-located WTD validation at observed well locations (assumes ~6 wells in-domain)

validation_design.comparison: co-located: simulated ZWT at well coordinates vs observed WTD time series (if available) or mean WTD
validation_design.metric: bias, RMSE, and correlation (if time series available)
validation_design.n_validation_points: 6 (assumed — depends on USGS well density in HUC 17030002)

validation_design.observation_source: Fan et al. 2013 equilibrium WTD prior (gridded)
validation_design.comparison: co-located: simulated ZWT at all column locations vs Fan 2013 WTD at same coordinates. Note: ELM 1-D equilibrium differs from Fan's lateral-flow equilibrium, so some bias is expected.
validation_design.metric: bias and spatial correlation across all columns

validation_design.comparison: Cannot validate directly. Compare simulated recharge distribution (mean, range, spatial pattern) to the published 500 mm/yr uniform assumption as a hypothesis test.
validation_design.metric: Descriptive statistics (mean, std dev, CV) and visual comparison of spatial pattern. Reject uniform assumption if CV > threshold (e.g. 0.2) or systematic elevation/soil trends are significant.

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: Baseline: NLDAS forcing 1980-2018 (full period for interannual variability), native SSURGO soil at each location, WTD-informed warm start from Fan 2013 prior, 5-year analysis period after warm start (total 6 years: 1 warm-start year + 5 analysis years)

requires_capabilities.capability: WTD-informed warm start from Fan 2013 prior
requires_capabilities.why: Recharge (QDRAI) is meaningless without realistic initial water table. Cold start at uniform 8.8 m WTD produces years of spin-up artifact. Fan 2013 WTD provides equilibrium initial condition for each column.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Meaningful recharge comparison and water table validation

requires_capabilities.capability: Multi-year ELM runs (6 years: 1 warm-start + 5 analysis)
requires_capabilities.why: Even with WTD warm start, root-zone soil moisture and aquifer storage need ~1 year to equilibrate. 5 analysis years provide robust mean recharge and interannual variability.

requires_capabilities.capability: SSURGO soil data ingest and per-column assignment
requires_capabilities.why: Soil texture is a primary driver. Each column needs site-specific hydraulic properties from SSURGO (or equivalent) rather than default uniform soil.

Provides elevation-resolved precipitation across the 1625 m relief (verified ~15 distinct precip values). Default Qian T62 (~1.9°) would give only ~2 values, insufficient to resolve elevation gradient.
NLDAS 12 km cells average over terrain. Ridgetop vs valley precipitation gradients are unresolved. High-resolution WRF or statistical downscaling with lapse rates would improve elevation control.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Fine-scale (<12 km) elevation effects on recharge

requires_capabilities.capability: Recharge observation dataset (lysimeters, tracers, or baseflow-derived estimates)
requires_capabilities.why: No direct recharge measurements available. Cannot validate QDRAI against observations, only test spatial pattern against uniform assumption.
Single-column ELM produces point recharge but no basin-integrated total. Cannot compare to streamflow-derived basin recharge or validate water balance closure.

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well location and WTD data ingest
requires_capabilities.why: Validation columns must be pinned to actual well coordinates. Need well locations (lat/lon) and observed WTD time series or mean values.

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM and elevation sampling at column locations
requires_capabilities.why: Elevation is a stratification axis and controls NLDAS forcing assignment. Need to extract elevation at each column location to verify stratum membership and forcing cell.

assumptions: USGS well density in HUC 17030002 is sufficient for validation (assumed ~6 wells; actual count unknown)
SSURGO soil data covers the domain and can be classified into coarse vs fine texture classes
NLDAS 0.125° forcing provides adequate orographic precipitation variation across the 1625 m relief (verified in prior work, but sub-12 km gradients are unresolved)
Fan 2013 WTD prior is available at column locations and can initialize ELM aquifer storage (clamped to 0.05-28.8 m range)
1-year warm start + 5-year analysis period is sufficient to stabilize recharge estimates (standard practice, but basin-specific spin-up time may vary)
The published 500 mm/yr uniform recharge claim is testable via spatial variability analysis (CV, elevation/soil trends) even without direct recharge observations
Forest is the dominant land cover across strata (typical for Cascades); columns avoid urban/water/steep areas
open_questions: What is the actual USGS well count and spatial distribution in HUC 17030002? Are well locations and WTD data accessible?
Are there any streamflow gages in or downstream of Naches that could provide basin-integrated recharge estimates via baseflow separation?
What is the source and context of the published 500 mm/yr uniform recharge claim? Is it a model assumption, a measurement-based estimate, or a regional average?
Is SNOTEL data available in or near the domain for snow validation (not listed in observations_available)?
Should the design include a sensitivity test of the warm-start method (Fan 2013 WTD vs cold start vs multi-year spin-up) to quantify initialization uncertainty?
What is the acceptable threshold for rejecting the uniform recharge assumption (e.g. CV > 0.2, or significant elevation trend p < 0.05)?
